cards.title: Structure a GA4 account and property for your store
cards.summary: Set up one GA4 account per business with a property that holds your website data, named and configured to match your store.
cards.use_when: You're creating GA4 for your first ecommerce store or onboarding a new store/brand into your existing Google setup.

cards.title: Review enhanced measurement instead of accepting defaults
cards.summary: GA4 auto-tracks page views, scrolls, outbound clicks, site search, forms, video and file downloads — audit these against what your store actually needs.
cards.use_when: You're finalizing the data stream for a store and deciding which automatic events should feed your reports.

cards.title: Create a thank-you-page event as a purchase-adjacent key event
cards.summary: Turn a confirmation/thank-you URL into a distinct key event without touching code, using GA4's Create Event.
cards.use_when: You want to count store conversions like completed lead forms or a thank-you page that isn't already covered by a purchase event.

cards.title: Deploy the GA4 tag via Google Tag Manager
cards.summary: Install GA4 on your store with a GTM Google Tag, a Constant variable for the Measurement ID, and an Initialization trigger.
cards.use_when: You're installing or re-installing GA4 tracking on a store site and want flexibility to add more tags later.

cards.title: Use Explore funnels for checkout drop-off analysis
cards.summary: Build a Funnel Exploration on begin_checkout → add_payment_info → purchase to see where shoppers abandon.
cards.use_when: You need to diagnose cart/checkout abandonment and pinpoint the step where shoppers drop out.

cards.title: Filter campaign rows out of a Free Form Explore report
cards.summary: Use the regex filter ^\(.*\)$ with 'Does Not Match Regex' to strip organic, direct and not-set rows so only named campaigns remain.
cards.use_when: You want an exploration report that shows only traffic from named UTM campaigns, without generic default-channel rows muddying the table.

cards.title: Choose User Acquisition vs Traffic Acquisition for the question at hand
cards.summary: User Acquisition attributes to the first source a user ever arrived from; Traffic Acquisition attributes to the session's most recent source.
cards.use_when: You're reporting on acquisition performance and need to decide whether you're evaluating first-touch brand discovery or per-session channel mix.

cards.title: Read the Monetization reports for purchase revenue, items, and list/promotion breakdowns
cards.summary: Use GA4 ecommerce reports to see purchase revenue, purchasers, items bought, list membership, promotions and coupon revenue.
cards.use_when: You're reviewing store revenue performance in GA4 and want to break down purchases by product, list placement or promotion code.

cards.title: Analyze landing page performance with the Landing Page report
cards.summary: See which pages are your top entry points and how many key events occur after users land on each one.
cards.use_when: You're deciding which entry pages to invest in, cross-promote or optimize for conversions.

cards.title: Compare Last Click and Data Driven attribution for channel decisions
cards.summary: The Key Event Attribution Models report shows each channel's key events and revenue under both Last Click and Data Driven models, plus the gap between them.
cards.use_when: You're deciding where to shift budget and need to see which channels last-click undervalues or overvalues.

cards.title: Enable Google Signals and extend data retention
cards.summary: Turn on Google Signals for demographics and Google Ads audience use, and extend GA4 data retention from the 2-month default to 14 months.
cards.use_when: You're configuring GA4 property settings and want richer audience reporting plus longer lookback in Explore reports.

cards.title: Build audiences in GA4 for retention and remarketing segmentation
cards.summary: Create custom audiences (e.g. users who haven't triggered a lead event) for reporting and for remarketing in linked Google Ads.
cards.use_when: You want to group users such as repeat purchasers or unconverted visitors for reporting, retargeting or lifecycle campaigns.

cards.title: Use GA4's realtime reports to sanity-check store launches and campaigns
cards.summary: Realtime Reports show pages, sources and events within seconds of arrival, useful for verifying a launch or campaign is landing correctly.
cards.use_when: You've just pushed a campaign email, ad or store change and want immediate confirmation that traffic is landing where you expect.

cards.title: Use Reports for monitoring and Explore for specific store questions
cards.summary: GA4 Reports are for ongoing monitoring of standard patterns; Explore is for answering a single analytical question with a custom view.
cards.use_when: You're deciding which part of GA4 to open for a given store question — a routine check or a diagnostic analysis.

cards.title: Distinguish Key Events in GA4 from Conversions in Google Ads
cards.summary: Advertising reports show both: Key Events are GA4 important actions, while Conversions are Google Ads conversion actions including imported GA4 events.
cards.use_when: You're reviewing advertising performance and trying to reconcile numbers between GA4 and Google Ads.

cards.title: Check audience size and budget projections in the Advertising reports
cards.summary: Advertising Segments shows how many users are available for targeting; Budgeting tools forecast conversions and spend under different budgets.
cards.use_when: You're planning paid acquisition spend and verifying remarketing audiences are large enough to be usable.

cards.title: Use DebugView to test store event implementation
cards.summary: DebugView shows a live feed of events as they're triggered from your site, letting you verify implementation before publishing changes.
cards.use_when: You've added or changed event tracking on your store and need to confirm events fire correctly before relying on them.

cards.title: Register custom dimensions and metrics for store-specific reporting
cards.summary: Custom Definitions let you surface parameters sent with events as usable dimensions or metrics in your GA4 reports.
cards.use_when: You're sending store-specific event parameters (e.g. membership tier, loyalty status) and want to slice reports by them.

cards.title: Create and use Comparisons as segment overlays on Reports
cards.summary: Comparisons are segments you apply to standard reports to compare user groups side by side.
cards.use_when: You want to see how one store segment performs against another within the same report, e.g. mobile vs desktop conversions.

cards.title: Use AI-driven insights and Analytics Advisor as starting points
cards.summary: GA4 surfaces automated insights on unusual changes and offers an AI chat interface to query the property's data.
cards.use_when: You've opened a store report and want a starting point for what's changed, or want a quick answer without building a report.

cards.title: Check data freshness expectations before acting on GA4 numbers
cards.summary: Realtime reports update within seconds, but standard reports can take 12–24 hours — set expectations on when store changes will be visible.
cards.use_when: You've just launched a campaign or event and are checking whether GA4 reports already reflect it.

cards.title: Verify the Platform dimension when blending web and app data
cards.summary: The Platform dimension shows whether each user came from the Web or App data stream — useful when a store runs both.
cards.use_when: Your store has both a website and a mobile app feeding the same property and you need to separate their metrics.

cards.title: Use User Attributes reports and treat 'not set' as unknown
cards.summary: User Attributes and Demographic Details expose country, city, gender, interests, age and language — with 'not set' meaning the value is unknown.
cards.use_when: You're profiling your store's audience for merchandising, content or campaign targeting decisions.

cards.title: Forecast with Analytics Advisor only as a first-pass input
cards.summary: The presenter demonstrates Analytics Advisor answering year-on-year performance questions from GA4 data.
cards.use_when: You need a quick baseline on store performance trends without building a report, e.g. before a monthly review.

cards.title: Redundant Meta Ads tracking: browser pixel plus server Conversions API
cards.summary: Meta's recommended setup fires the same event twice — once from the browser pixel and once from the server-side Conversions API — then merges them with deduplication.
cards.use_when: Planning or auditing the tracking architecture that feeds Meta Ads purchase and lead optimization for your store, e.g. after iOS/ad-blocker signal loss hurts reported ROAS.

cards.title: Get the two credentials the Conversions API setup requires
cards.summary: Meta Conversions API setup needs exactly two credentials from Events Manager: the pixel/dataset ID and a Conversions API access token.
cards.use_when: Starting a store's Meta Conversions API implementation and you need the identifiers to paste into GTM variables.

cards.title: Consent-gate the client-side Meta pixel so it fires on the same page as opt-in
cards.summary: Require marketing/storage consent on the pixel tag and trigger it on the cookie-consent-update event so opt-in is recorded on the first page view rather than only on the next page.
cards.use_when: Formatting the client-side pixel tag in GTM for a store with a cookie banner, where you need Meta to receive the event on the page where the shopper actually consents.

cards.title: Send Meta store events server-side with the Conversions API template
cards.summary: Configure server-side GTM tags with the Facebook Conversions API template, overriding event names, wiring token and pixel variables, and gating on consent.
cards.use_when: Building the server-side half of a store's Meta tracking, for example sending PageView and a form/purchase-style conversion event through the Conversions API.

cards.title: Automate the Meta test event ID with a Debug Mode lookup table
cards.summary: A GTM lookup table keyed on Debug Mode supplies the Meta test event code only in preview, so a forgotten test ID can never leak into production and suppress live conversion data.
cards.use_when: Testing Meta Conversions API tags in a live store, where forgetting to remove a hard-coded test event code would silently divert real conversions into the test screen.

cards.title: Deduplicate Meta events by passing one Event ID into both streams
cards.summary: The Conversions API and the browser pixel only merge when both carry the identical Event ID, which Meta uses to collapse the duplicate into one event.
cards.use_when: Finishing a redundant Meta tracking setup on a store so that each page view and conversion is counted once, not twice.

cards.title: Verification checks that both Meta tracking streams land and merge
cards.summary: A three-place check — server container preview, tag success status, and Events Manager — confirms the Conversions API is correctly receiving deduplicated events.
cards.use_when: After deploying or editing Meta tracking tags for a store, before trusting the reported conversion counts.

cards.title: Separate sales-based marketing revenue from actual cash receipts
cards.summary: Label the source revenue proxy clearly and reconcile actual receipts separately.
cards.use_when: Reconciling revenue for marketing spend decisions or profit calculations on your Shopify store.

cards.title: Revenue Troubleshooting Framework: Sessions x Conversion Rate x AOV
cards.summary: Use the decomposition Total Sales = Sessions x Conversion Rate x AOV to diagnose the root cause of any revenue dip in your Shopify store.
cards.use_when: When revenue drops or spikes unexpectedly, to pinpoint the specific metric causing the change.

cards.title: Cross-check Shopify attribution before reallocating spend
cards.summary: Treat the presenter's skepticism as a prompt to triangulate channel evidence, not a blanket instruction to discard Shopify reports.
cards.use_when: When analyzing marketing channel performance or deciding where to allocate ad spend.

cards.title: Use Cohort Analysis Instead of Shopify's Returning Customer Rate
cards.summary: Shopify's 'Returning Customer Rate' is misleading for gauging loyalty; use cohort analysis for accurate retention and lifetime value insights.
cards.use_when: When evaluating customer loyalty, retention, or predicting long-term revenue from a cohort.

cards.title: Funnel Drop-off Ratios: 4:2:1 and 2:1:1
cards.summary: Analyze Shopify's funnel breakdown (Add to Cart, Reach Checkout, Purchase) against benchmark ratios to identify conversion optimization opportunities.
cards.use_when: When optimizing checkout flow or diagnosing where customers abandon the purchase process.

cards.title: Average Order Value: Context and Limitations
cards.summary: Shopify's AOV metric excludes shipping charges and is a mean, not median; use it as a top-line indicator but dig deeper before making changes.
cards.use_when: When assessing pricing, bundling, or upsell strategies, or when AOV appears in revenue troubleshooting.

cards.title: Sessions Discrepancy: Shopify vs. Google Analytics 4
cards.summary: Shopify's session count often includes bot traffic, inflating numbers compared to GA4; cross-reference both for accurate traffic and conversion rate analysis.
cards.use_when: When analyzing traffic trends or calculating conversion rates, especially if you suspect bot traffic or see unexplained dips.

cards.title: Product Sell-Through Rate for Inventory Planning
cards.summary: Track sell-through rate at product and category levels to optimize inventory, cash flow, and sustainable growth.
cards.use_when: When planning inventory purchases, managing cash conversion cycle, or deciding which products to reorder or discontinue.

cards.title: Customizing the Shopify Analytics Dashboard
cards.summary: The default Shopify Analytics dashboard contains many misleading or unhelpful metrics; customize it to focus on actionable data.
cards.use_when: When setting up your Shopify analytics for the first time or when overwhelmed by irrelevant metrics.

cards.title: Identifying Bot Traffic via Location Report
cards.summary: Use Shopify's 'Sessions by location' report to detect bot traffic spikes from specific cities, which can skew session and conversion metrics.
cards.use_when: When you suspect inflated sessions or unexplained conversion rate changes, especially if traffic sources seem off.

cards.title: Orders vs. Orders Fulfilled for Operational Health
cards.summary: Monitor the gap between orders and orders fulfilled to track unshipped orders and fulfillment efficiency.
cards.use_when: When assessing fulfillment operations, identifying backlog, or communicating with customers about shipping delays.

cards.title: Sales Channel Breakdown for Accountability
cards.summary: Use Shopify's 'Sales by channel' report to separate online store revenue from other channels like POS or Shop app.
cards.use_when: When managing multi-channel sales or holding marketing partners accountable for online store performance.

cards.title: Zero-party vs first-party vs third-party data
cards.summary: Define the three data tiers and recognize that first-party tracking often misattributes the true source of a conversion.
cards.use_when: When deciding which customer data to collect and trust for store merchandising, acquisition channel decisions, or attribution reporting.

cards.title: Use post-purchase surveys as another attribution signal
cards.summary: Ask customers how they discovered the store and compare their responses with tracked touchpoints; neither is ground truth.
cards.use_when: When platform attribution (e.g., a Google Ads dashboard claiming a sale) disagrees with what customers say, or when setting acquisition budget allocation.

cards.title: Prioritize the 3% most loyal and 3% most dissatisfied customers
cards.summary: A source rule of thumb: mine qualitative feedback primarily from your most devoted and most unhappy customers.
cards.use_when: When gathering customer feedback for product development, PDP copy, or retention offers and you cannot survey the whole base.

cards.title: Avoid HiPPO decision-making
cards.summary: The Highest Paid Person's Opinion can cherry-pick data to confirm biases instead of letting raw data drive strategy.
cards.use_when: When an executive or founder wants to change pricing, merchandising, or channel spend based on conviction rather than evidence.

cards.title: Distinguish compounding metrics from linear metrics
cards.summary: Some metrics compound over time (conversion rate, referral coefficient) while others scale linearly, so they deserve different investment logic.
cards.use_when: When allocating effort between acquisition, retention, and referral programs, or when explaining why a metric's improvement is worth more than it appears.

cards.title: Reconcile platform attribution with self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Expect and plan for the gap between what ad platforms claim and what customers say drove the purchase.
cards.use_when: When Google Ads or a social platform reports conversions that zero-party survey data does not corroborate, and you must decide budget.

cards.title: Test incrementality instead of trusting attribution
cards.summary: Use holdout and incrementality tests to determine whether spend actually caused sales attribution claims.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to scale, cut, or keep a paid channel whose platform-reported ROAS may be inflated.

cards.title: Capture the 'why' behind quantitative results with qualitative tools
cards.summary: Use session and feedback tools like Hotjar alongside surveys to explain the reasons attribution numbers cannot.
cards.use_when: When checkout or PDP conversion is underperforming and you need the reason, not just the rate.

cards.title: Two Ground Rules Before Investing in Ecommerce Analytics
cards.summary: Data analytics only pays off when metrics are measured before you need them and every report ends in a decision, not a dashboard.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether your store is ready to spend on analytics tools or headcount, or auditing why your current reporting isn't changing any store decisions.

cards.title: Qualitative vs Quantitative Ecommerce Data: What and Why
cards.summary: Quantitative data tells you what changed on your store; qualitative data tells you why customers acted, and both are needed.
cards.use_when: Interpreting a conversion-rate change on a PDP or landing page and deciding what to fix next.

cards.title: Zero, First and Third-Party Data for Ecommerce Attribution
cards.summary: Zero-party data is what customers tell you, first-party is what you track, third-party is external enrichment — and they frequently disagree.
cards.use_when: Reconciling attribution across ad platforms, post-purchase surveys and CRM data, or planning what customer attributes to enrich for segmentation.

cards.title: Collect Customer Feedback at Every Lifecycle Stage
cards.summary: Ask customers questions before purchase, after purchase and after churn — not just at checkout — because founders who stop talking to customers weekly lose the why.
cards.use_when: Designing a voice-of-customer program to feed PDP copy, merchandising, retention and win-back campaigns.

cards.title: The 3% Rule for Qualitative Feedback
cards.summary: Focus qualitative listening on your 3% most loyal and 3% most dissatisfied customers rather than the 94% in the middle.
cards.use_when: Choosing which customers to interview or survey when you have limited research time and need the highest-signal input for product, offer or retention decisions.

cards.title: Don't Let the HiPPO Pick Your Ecommerce Metrics
cards.summary: Using data to defend a pre-existing opinion (Highest Paid Person's Opinion) suppresses profitable tests — build the test and let results, not titles, decide.
cards.use_when: When a founder, CMO or director overrides a proposed test on brand or 'that's how we've always done it' grounds — e.g., homepage merchandising, product imagery or promotion placement.

cards.title: Pick One Primary Metric: Customers, Revenue or Profit
cards.summary: A company can typically optimize for only one of three top-level metrics at a time — customers, revenue or profit — and each sub-metric should ladder to it.
cards.use_when: Setting the quarter's focus for acquisition, pricing or cost decisions, or resolving arguments between departments optimizing different numbers.

cards.title: Match KPI Focus to Your Company Stage
cards.summary: Early-stage stores optimize for customer count and can lose money doing it; mature or steady stores can shift to profit and cost reduction.
cards.use_when: Deciding ad spend, discount depth and growth targets for a store that has found product-market fit versus one that is happy with its market.

cards.title: Compounders vs Linear Metrics in Ecommerce
cards.summary: Conversion rate and referral coefficient compound revenue and customer growth, so prioritize them over one-off linear levers.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest next month's budget in CRO, referral program, or a linear traffic/spend increase.

cards.title: Watch What Your Winning Metric Breaks
cards.summary: Optimizing one metric can quietly damage lifetime value, customer quality or brand, so track the metrics your decision touches.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a conversion tactic with brand or quality side effects — misspelled-ad testing, aggressive discounting, or AOV-boosting bundles.

cards.title: When to Change KPIs: The Top-of-S-Curve Test
cards.summary: Change your core focus when additional spend on your best lever returns less and less — not on a weekly or monthly whim.
cards.use_when: Reviewing whether to keep pushing CRO, shift budget to LTV/retention work, or reallocate to acquisition channels.

cards.title: Predictive Analytics and AI Execution in Ecommerce
cards.summary: Analytics has moved from humans explaining charts to AI recommending actions — and increasingly executing them — so stores that adopt predictive tools and AI-run tests are positioned to outcompete slower adopters.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to apply AI in merchandising, ad creative, attribution, on-site conversion or customer service, or fending off 'AI will hurt our brand' objections.

cards.title: Start Collecting Store Data Before It's Worth Anything
cards.summary: The value of an early data set is optionality: you can't analyze history you never recorded, so log data points now that only pay off at larger scale.
cards.use_when: Setting up tracking, CRM fields or operational records for a store that hasn't started paid acquisition or advanced analytics yet.

cards.title: Plan ecommerce roles around AI-resistant work
cards.summary: Structure ecommerce team hiring and personal skill development toward strategy, AI tool operation and tech understanding rather than automatable low-level tasks.
cards.use_when: Deciding what roles to hire for in your store (analyst, ads buyer, content creator) or which skills to build so your work survives the next few years.

cards.title: Use an independent tool directory before buying ecommerce software
cards.summary: Browse an independent review directory of 260+ ecommerce tools to understand ecosystem categories before choosing stack components.
cards.use_when: Evaluating or replacing a store tool — analytics, email, reviews, subscriptions — and wanting category context before committing budget.

cards.title: Decide Whether a Product Needs an Advertorial (Three-Minute Rule)
cards.summary: Use the source's 'three-minute explanation' heuristic plus awareness and market conditions to decide between direct PDP traffic and an advertorial pre-sell.
cards.use_when: Choosing the landing destination for cold paid traffic for a specific product, before building creative or a funnel.

cards.title: Six Advertorial Formats and the Obstacle Each Solves
cards.summary: Map each of the source's six advertorial formats to the specific buyer obstacle it is designed to overcome.
cards.use_when: Selecting which advertorial angle to write when cold-traffic conversion is blocked by a known objection.

cards.title: Buyer's Guide Advertorial That Pre-Sells the Click
cards.summary: Build a 'Top 5' comparison advertorial that names and discredits competitors so the featured product arrives pre-sold.
cards.use_when: Running cold or retargeting traffic in a crowded category where the buyer is comparison shopping or skeptical.

cards.title: Scandal/Whistleblower Advertorial Structure
cards.summary: Position a small brand against a corrupt industry to convert distrustful buyers using a discovery-and-shortcut narrative.
cards.use_when: Selling in a category where consumers distrust incumbents (beauty, health, supplements) and need a reason to trust a smaller brand.

cards.title: Case Study Advertorial That Burns Down Alternatives
cards.summary: Use a detailed single-case narrative to discredit every standard solution before presenting the product.
cards.use_when: Selling a solution to a chronic problem where buyers have already tried and failed with conventional treatments.

cards.title: Universal Advertorial Block Structure
cards.summary: Assemble any advertorial from a fixed sequence of blocks: hook, identify reader, agitate, discredit alternatives, prove, reveal offer, handle objections, guarantee, CTA.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing an advertorial draft for any product or format.

cards.title: Three Layers of Proof: Mechanism, Social, Demonstration
cards.summary: Ensure every advertorial carries all three proof types and make social proof specific and continuity-focused.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an advertorial draft for weak or missing credibility elements before launch.

cards.title: Place Four CTAs Across the Advertorial
cards.summary: Distribute calls to action after the hook, mechanism, proof, and objections/guarantee rather than only at the bottom.
cards.use_when: Deciding CTA placement and count on a long-form advertorial page.

cards.title: Advertorial Funnel KPIs and Optimization Sequence
cards.summary: Set funnel benchmarks of roughly 30–40% advertorial-to-PDP click-through and about 15% checkout conversion, then optimize stage by stage.
cards.use_when: Monitoring a live advertorial funnel and deciding which metric to fix first.

cards.title: Research Awareness Level and Objections Before Writing
cards.summary: Diagnose the target audience's awareness level and real objections before choosing a format or writing copy.
cards.use_when: Starting a new advertorial for a product, before writing any blocks.

cards.title: Model Existing Live Advertorials Instead of Starting From Scratch
cards.summary: Find high-performing advertorials already running in your niche and model their structure rather than designing from zero.
cards.use_when: Looking for proven structures and angles to adapt before writing a new advertorial.

cards.title: Build Advertorials Fast: One Day, Cheap Build, No Overthinking
cards.summary: Write in blocks, hand off the technical build, and ship within roughly a day rather than planning for months.
cards.use_when: Ready to produce and launch an advertorial page without over-engineering production.

cards.title: Targeted social proof placement at the point of action
cards.summary: Match handpicked testimonials to the top buying objections and place them next to Add to Cart and bundle selectors.
cards.use_when: Designing a PDP or landing page and deciding which testimonials to show and where to position them.

cards.title: Let images sell: visual value proposition on the page
cards.summary: Because most users skim text and absorb images first, make product imagery carry the emotional, social and functional benefits.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing PDP and landing page imagery when users skim past copy.
